restrictions: Two distinct 135-byte messages M(t) = U || 0^40 || U || 0^15, U the 40 little-endian bytes of a 320-bit parameter t, so that with SHA3 padding (byte 135 = 0x86) each message is one absorbed block. t ranges over the cosets t_j + span(W40), j < 256 G, of the 40-dimensional field W40 listed in proof.md Section 3, with origins t_j drawn as fresh randomness (two independent uniform random 256-bit words per coset, Section 6.1) and the fixed Gray order of each coset.

Complete SHA3-256 sponge of sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1: zero initial state, rate 136 bytes, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 5 of Keccak-f[1600] in the single permutation call, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with reference operation cost 1626: a six-round permutation is one unit, every other operation 1/1626 (no permutation call is made: verification evaluates the six rounds in 1452 word operations); generated straight-line code with immediate addresses, its generation charged in preprocessing (proof.md Section 5.1). N = G F_g + G (4664 2^40 + 175 (2^40 - 1)) + G S_g + 9 Q + 3127 R140 + (2^70 + 16 + 7660) = 13764968169381848226007825243795404468360 word operations (Section 10), with the bit-sliced setup S_g = 8530343036056 per group (Section 6.5); time_log2 = 122.67102 is log2(N/1626) rounded up, by the integer certificate 1626^100000 2^12267101 <= N^100000 < 1626^100000 2^12267102.

Memory below 2^141 words, 2^146 bytes: a direct sparse array of 2^140 words that is never initialized (the sparse-set table, indexed by the candidate identifier, is correct for any initial memory, Lemma 8), a dense array of Q words, coset records (the retained random origins), a work region with a per-group buffer of 175 (2^40 - 1) words, and generated code (Section 11.1). Preprocessing at most 2^70 + 16 + 7660 word operations (below 2^59.34 target compressions), included in time_log2: code generation, constants, byte tables, the certificate and the search that produced W40 (Section 11.2). No advice.

Success at least 0.39 is a probability over the algorithm's fresh coins (the random coset origins, drawn by a leader step charged at its 11 operations per coset and 5 per group) and rests on one declared heuristic, H_coset: over those coins the occupancy, key-match and triple bounds of proof.md Section 9 hold (Section 12). Proved in proof.md: two-round affinity on every coset of W40 (780-polarization certificate, recomputed by the experiment), degree at most 8 before the last chi, exactness of the Gray-order finite differences and of their initialization, the sparse-set table for arbitrary initial memory, the duplicate-coset bound C(256 G, 2) 2^-280 < 2.5e-32 in the failure budget, detection up to a bounded triple event, and every operation count.

No full-scale run and no collision are claimed. The declared experiment executes the schedule at a reduced size (256 cosets per group, origins from each trial's own coins, the first 2^9 Gray points of each coset, the full 140-bit key and table) through a counting machine and stops unless every executed count equals the formula of proof.md; its outputs are not evidence of cost, and its own_pairs16 count checks the premise only at 16 bits.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. CAMP's coins are the C = 256 G coset origins t_j (G = 1202736947187009950184717), independent and uniform on F_2^320, each drawn from two calls of the cost model's primitive 'independent uniform random 256-bit word' (proof.md Section 6.1). For the Q = 2^48 G messages they generate, with the fixed Gray enumeration of span(W40) inside each coset in CAMP's order, let D be the event that the C cosets are distinct (Pr[not D] <= C(C, 2) 2^-280 < 2.5e-32, proved, Lemma 7), F1 the event that no two messages share a digest, X the number of unordered pairs with equal 140-bit keys and Y the number of bad triples (Lemma 9). Assume, over the coins: (a) Pr[F1 | D] <= 1/T40 with T40 = sum_{k<=40} lambda^k/k! and lambda = Q(Q - 1)/2^257; (b) E[X | D] <= Q(Q - 1)/2^141 and Var[X | D] <= Q(Q - 1)/2^141; (c) E[Y | D] <= lambda (Q - 2)/2^140. These are the values that independent uniform digests of distinct messages give. Then the failure probability over the fresh coins is at most Pr[not D] + 1/T40 + 1/4096 (Chebyshev at the verification cap R140) + lambda (Q - 2)/2^140 (Markov) < 61/100 (exact rational comparison; G is the least group count for which it holds), so the success probability is greater than 0.3900000000000000000000000848 (proof.md Section 9).
heuristics.scope: The randomized campaign at full size: C = 256 G independent uniform coset origins drawn by the algorithm, complete 40-dimensional cosets of span(W40) in the fixed Gray order, the full 256-bit digest and its 140-bit key projection, conditioned on distinct cosets. The success probability is over these fresh coins for the fixed target. Nothing else in the claim is heuristic: two-round affinity, the degree bound, the exactness of the enumeration, the sparse-set table, the duplicate-coset bound and every operation count are proved in proof.md Sections 3 to 7, 9 and 10.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured on the target function in three preregistered batches at six rounds (protocol texts with their SHA-256, the GPU program, its driver, the run scripts and the raw result lines are in proof.md Appendix A; pass rule: every count at least expected - 4 sigma; no reruns): 17 runs of 2^30 real six-round SHA3-256 digests, exact equal-pair counts of 32-bit within-coset and 44-bit global projections of each of the four digest lanes. Batches 1 and 2 (13 runs) drew their coset origins uniformly at random, as CAMP does, with complete cosets of 2^20, 2^24 and 2^28 messages of random subspaces of span(W40) and random-direction controls; they are the direct evidence for the premise over random origins. Batch 3 used fixed origins with the first 20 or 24 ordered W40 vectors. All counts lie within 2.1 sigma of expectation and none below expected - 1.4 sigma; a fourth batch at five rounds (context only) also passes. The extrapolation is from single-lane 32- and 44-bit projections on 2^30 messages to the 256-bit digest and its 140-bit key, from 20- to 28-dimensional subspaces to complete 40-dimensional cosets, and to Q = 2^48 G messages in 256 G random cosets; projected pair counts at this size do not establish 256-bit behaviour.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption: no proof is known, and image size or balance do not imply it (a balanced linear map can be injective on every translate of a campaign space). On each coset every digest bit has degree at most 16 in the 40 inner variables, a real structure; the tests found no pair deficit at the tested widths but reach neither 256 bits nor complete cosets, and no full collision is observed. The premise evidence is our own GPU runs, validated against the organizer reference but not executed by the organizer. The organizer-run experiment checks the premise only through a 16-bit pair count on each trial's own 512 digests (own_pairs16); it executes the schedule at a reduced size and the organizer recomputes the digests of returned pairs (none expected).
